title: Client-side versus server-side rendering: what changes for testing

videos.script: The same shop can be built in two ways. {{two-pages}} On the home page, the browser builds the list. The HTML arrives empty, and a script fills it in. On the new page, the server writes the products into the HTML before it sends it. {{curl}} Ask both pages with curl, which runs no script. One answer has no products. The other has all eight. {{timeline}} But arriving is not the same as working. The buttons on the server's page are drawn at once. The script that makes them work comes a second and a half later. {{test}} A test that clicks straight away passes every check Playwright makes. The button is visible, and it is enabled. And the basket stays at zero. Five runs, five failures. {{wait}} So the test waits for the right signal, a marker the page sets when it is ready. Better still, the developers can disable the buttons until then. {{no-script}} Then you switch JavaScript off, and see which page still shows its fruit. {{layers}} And you choose the cheapest layer for each check. Some checks need no browser at all.
